# `recursive-call`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: disciplined · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports direct recursion and proven two-function mutual recursion in the scanned
project.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Recursion makes stack consumption depend on input depth; an explicit worklist
makes the resource visible and boundable.

## When it fires

Reported mutual cycles name both functions, which must be declared in the same
file, since an unqualified call names a declaration of its own file. Recursion
no runtime input can deepen is exempt: `inline` functions, functions returning
`type`, `comptime_int`, or `comptime_float` (every call runs at compile time),
functions whose parameters are all `comptime` (no runtime argument reaches
them), and calls inside `comptime` blocks or expressions. So is recursion an
explicit bound limits: the function checks a depth counter that every
recursive call advances (`if (depth >= 32) return false;` and
`walk(child, depth + 1)`), or a budget it passes on, where failing the check
leaves the function (`try require(remaining.* != 0)`,
`budget.charge(depth) catch return false`). A budget is a pointer named
`budget`, `remaining` or `fuel`, typed `*...Budget`, or an integer the body
counts down. A count down to zero by value (`fact(n - 1)`) and a cursor
counting up through the input are input-controlled and still reported, as is
recursion through `anytype` parameters, since a self-referential type can
repeat an instantiation at run time. Like the other
disciplined-profile rules it skips `test` blocks, private functions only tests
call, and test, fuzz, and script files.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn fact(n: u64) u64 {
    if (n == 0) return 1;
    return n * fact(n - 1);
}
```
